messages.subject: Re: vectorization error checking
parts:
On 8/8/12 12:27 AM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> Just to let you know, I got the check working for check_greater().
> I'll implement the rest of the checks with 2 or more types this week.

Awesome! (And harder than it sounds given all
the overloading, template specialization, and compound
template parameters winging around -- I was stuck on
some nasty ordering interactions.)

For everyone else, this means we can use
Eigen vectors or row vectors in vectorized normals.
We'll have the same for other distributions as they get
vectorized. I already have the manual description in
the vectorization section of the optimization chapter.

Here's a simple regression with improper priors:

data {
int[0,] N;
vector[N] y;
matrix[N,K] x;
}
parameters {
real[0,] sigma;
vector[K] beta;
}
model {
y ~ normal(x * beta, sigma);
}

The implementation Marcus did for matrix and vector products
will also be a big win here. We could even go further and
write a function normal_regression_log(y,x,beta,sigma) and
push one step further through the matrix-vector product.

Something tells me we're about to vectorize inv_logit :-)

> It relies on VectorView-ing either a double or vector (generic, as in
> std::vector or Eigen::Matrix). I don't see anything wrong with it, but
> do you think we'll take a performance hit on using it? If so, I can
> avoid VectorView by writing more functions.

VectorView requires a constructor call, which in turn requires
an assignment. But it doesn't need a malloc/free. Given
the loop bounds are known statically, they should get unrolled
along with the indexes, so there shouldn't be a cost beyond
the constructor.

We already pay the VectorView constructor price in the vectorized
normal, so if we use those instances, there shouldn't be any
additional penalty. (This is one reason why Matt's implementation
of the vectorization was so efficient, by the way.)

- Bob
